findings.issue_text: [BUG] The new feature-flag-gated ClientRemovedEvent handler calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false), but when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled the management() factory returns MgmtPermissionsV2, whose ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled() (ClientPermissionsV2.java lines ~140-142) unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException. Deleting any client in a realm where the V2 admin authz path is active throws UnsupportedOperationException from inside the ProviderEventListener during ClientRemovedEvent dispatch, so client deletion fails (or corrupts the deletion transaction) instead of cleaning up fine-grained permission resources — the same applies to the RoleRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent branches if the V2 roles()/groups() implementations also throw, since the entire listener body is now gated on exactly the feature flag that activates V2.

[ADVISORY] The listener body is wrapped in if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)) with no visible import of org.keycloak.common.Profile added in this diff hunk. If AdminPermissions.java did not previously import Profile (no import line appears in the changed hunk), the file does not compile; even if it was already imported, the gating silently skips permission-resource cleanup for realms whose permissions were enabled while the feature was on and then the feature was disabled, leaking authz resources whose names reference deleted clients/users/groups.

[BUG] setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException, so the ClientRemovedEvent handler registered in AdminPermissions.registerListener crashes under V2, breaking client deletion. The listener added in AdminPermissions.java calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false) on ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent; with MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() now returning ClientPermissionsV2, this throws UnsupportedOperationException from inside the event listener, aborting client removal with a 500 for every admin running the V2 permissions stack with ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ enabled.

[BUG] canExchangeTo and exchangeToPermission throw UnsupportedOperationException with no V2 replacement, silently dropping the token-exchange authorization requirement for clients. Any deployment relying on per-client token-exchange permissions (the TOKEN_EXCHANGE flow exercised via AdminPermissionManagement.TOKEN_EXCHANGE, imported but unused here) gets a hard runtime exception instead of an evaluation once V2 is active; the requirement 'restrict which clients can be exchanged to' has no implementation in the V2 path and no test in the diff covers it.

[ADVISORY] The per-client hasPermission fallback to the all-clients resource only triggers when the per-client resource is absent; a stale per-client resource with no attached policies skips the all-clients grant. An admin who once created a resource-scoped permission on a specific client (creating the named resource) and later deletes the permission but the resource lingers will be denied even when a valid all-clients permission exists, because the findByResource(...).isEmpty() check is only inside the resource == null branch; the next person bitten is the admin doing per-client to realm-wide permission migration.

[ADVISORY] The new MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope is never exercised by any test in the diff. testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient grants Set.of(MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, CONFIGURE) and asserts role-mapping and composite-mapping, but no test anywhere asserts the canMapClientScopeRoles(ClientModel) path (adding/removing available client scopes for role mapping), so a regression in that overridden method would pass CI silently.

[ADVISORY] The private getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken) method is dead code — its only consumer (canExchangeTo) was replaced with a throw. Readers and maintainers of the token-exchange path get a false signal that client-identity evaluation still happens here; the method and the ClientModelIdentity/DefaultEvaluationContext imports should be deleted along with the unsupported exchange methods or restored when exchange is implemented.

[ADVISORY] The V2 overrides for client-scope evaluation (canManageClientScopes, canManage(ClientScopeModel), canView(ClientScopeModel)) have no test coverage in the diff. PermissionClientTest tests client-level and all-clients permissions but never asserts the client-scope variants (e.g. admin console listing/managing realm client scopes under V2), so the realmResourceServer-null and hasOneAdminRole short-circuit branches in these three overridden methods are unverified and a regression would only surface as an admin-console 403 in production.

[BUG] hasPermission(ClientModel, scope) never consults the all-clients (type-level) grant once a per-client resource exists, so a realm-wide permission is silently ignored for any client that already has a per-client resource. An admin who is granted MANAGE/VIEW on all Clients (testManageAllClients pattern) is denied operations on any specific client for which a per-client resource was previously created (e.g. by an earlier CONFIGURE- or MAP_ROLES-scoped permission), because findByName(client.getId()) succeeds and evaluation runs only against that resource's scopes; the all-clients fallback branch is unreachable.

[BUG] The ClientRemovedEvent handler calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false), which ClientPermissionsV2 overrides to throw UnsupportedOperationException, so deleting any client under the V2 permissions stack throws. With ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (and the V2 permissions path) enabled, every client deletion fires ClientRemovedEvent, the listener calls the V2 evaluator's setPermissionsEnabled, and the UnsupportedOperationException propagates — client deletion returns a 500 instead of cleaning up (or cleanly skipping) authorization resources.

[ADVISORY] canExchangeTo and exchangeToPermission throw UnsupportedOperationException while the interface contract (ClientPermissionEvaluator.canExchangeTo) is retained, leaving in-tree callers on a hard failure. Token-exchange permission checks that route through ClientPermissionEvaluator (e.g. admin/grant-type token exchange authorization paths) hit a raw UnsupportedOperationException under V2 — a 500/stack trace rather than a deny or a feature-flagged 501 — so operators enabling the new Client resource type lose working token-exchange admin endpoints.

[ADVISORY] getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken) is dead code — its only conceivable caller (canExchangeTo) throws UnsupportedOperationException, so the method is unreachable from this class. Future readers assume client-identity evaluation is wired up when it is not; the next change to V2 token-exchange support has to rediscover that this path was never exercised, and the unused method plus its imports (ClientModelIdentity, DefaultEvaluationContext, AccessToken) survive as misleading surface.

[ADVISORY] The new MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope and the canMapClientScopeRoles path it exists to serve are added in this diff but no test in the diff grants or exercises map-roles-client-scope. testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient grants MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE and CONFIGURE but never MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE, so a regression in ClientPermissionsV2.canMapClientScopeRoles (or in the schema scope registration) ships silently — admins granted client-scope role mapping get silent 403s with no test failing.

[BUG] hasPermission(ClientModel, String) dereferences a possibly-null all-clients resource when the per-client resource does not exist. When no per-client resource exists and AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource returns null for the Clients type (no 'all clients' resource has been created yet), authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, null) is called with a null resource, producing a NullPointerException/500 on every client permission check instead of the clean 'deny' the method is supposed to return — the common case for a realm that has never configured an all-clients permission.

[ADVISORY] V2 overrides setPermissionsEnabled/isPermissionsEnabled/resource/etc. to throw UnsupportedOperationException while the global AdminPermissions.registerListener (this same diff) still calls clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false) on every ClientRemovedEvent under ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ. Any code path that routes the ClientRemovedEvent/RoleRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent cleanup through MgmtPermissionsV2 (i.e. whenever V2 is the active management implementation) crashes client/role/group deletion with UnsupportedOperationException, so deleting a client becomes a 500 instead of a cleanup. Rebuttal: 'V1 and V2 are gated by different flags so the listener never sees V2' — but the listener gate in this diff is exactly ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ and nothing in the diff shows the V2 selection is a different flag, so the mismatch is at minimum an undocumented coupling that the next flag change trips.

[BUG] Wrapping the entire event listener in Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) changes cleanup semantics: previously the role/client/group removal cleanup ran unconditionally, now it is skipped entirely when the feature is disabled. A realm that had fine-grained admin permissions, then has the feature disabled (a supported profile change), accumulates stale authorization resources/policies on every subsequent role, client, and group deletion; when the feature is re-enabled those stale grants evaluate against deleted entities. The old code deliberately cleaned up in the disabled state; the new guard removes that safety net.

[ADVISORY] getClientsWithPermission iterates every Clients-typed resource and runs a full policy evaluation (root.evaluatePermission) per resource, an N-evaluation loop that does not short-circuit or batch. Realms with many clients and client-scoped permissions pay one full authorization-policy evaluation per client resource on every call to this method (used to compute which clients a limited admin can see), turning client listing into an O(N × policy-graph) operation that degrades linearly with realm client count.

[ADVISORY] getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken) is dead code: its only consumer was the token-exchange path, and canExchangeTo in this same class is now an unconditional throw. The next maintainer of token-exchange-in-V2 assumes the evaluation-context plumbing exists and is wired, when it is unreachable; it should be deleted with the other unused exchange plumbing rather than kept as a fossil.

[ADVISORY] The permission-scope matching loop (iterate permissions, iterate scopes, compare against expectedScopes) is copy-pasted three times across hasPermission(ClientModel,String), hasPermission(String), and hasGrantedPermission. Three hand-maintained copies of the same matching logic (one already drifting: two use expectedScopes.contains, one uses scope.equals) — a future fix to matching semantics (e.g. scope name normalization) must be applied in three places or the copies silently diverge into inconsistent authorization decisions.

[ADVISORY] canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles/canMapClientScopeRoles grant access only via per-client MAP_ROLES_* permissions, with no admin-role or MANAGE fallback the way canManage/canView have. An admin holding the MANAGE_CLIENTS admin role gets canManage(client)==true but canMapRoles(client)==false; any caller that consults canMapRoles directly (role-mapping endpoints that do not first short-circuit on canManage) denies a role the V1 evaluator and the interface javadoc ('true if caller has MANAGE_CLIENTS') say the admin should have — a semantic gap between the documented contract and the V2 implementation.

[BUG] MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() returns ClientPermissionsV2, but the shared ProviderEventListener registered in AdminPermissions.registerListener unconditionally calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false) on ClientRemovedEvent, which this class implements as `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")`. In any deployment where the V2 evaluator is active together with ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ enabled, deleting a client fires ClientRemovedEvent, the listener reaches ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled, and the UnsupportedOperationException propagates out of the event dispatch, failing the client-deletion admin request (500) and leaving the client undeletable — the review iteration that wired MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() into the existing cleanup listener silently broke the cleanup contract those call sites depend on.

[ADVISORY] The diff wraps the entire pre-existing RoleRemovedEvent/ClientRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent cleanup listener in `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ))`, changing the behavior of the existing V1 listener path even though the PR's stated intent is only to add the Client resource type to the schema. Any realm/operator relying on the previous unconditional cleanup (e.g. where permissionsEnabled flags or authorization resources were previously cleared on role/client/group removal regardless of the profile check) now silently retains stale permission state when the feature flag is off; this objective change to the V1 cleanup semantics was not part of the announced intent and needs explicit acceptance.

[ADVISORY] In hasPermission(ClientModel, String), when no per-client resource exists, the fallback loads the all-clients type resource and only checks `findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty()` before evaluating — it never verifies that the matching policies actually grant the requested scope at the policy-attachment stage, and it also silently treats an empty-but-present policy set as denial via evaluation, duplicating scope-matching logic already present in hasGrantedPermission (parallel hand-maintained permission-matching blocks: hasPermission(client,...), hasPermission(String), and hasGrantedPermission each re-implement the same evaluate-and-match-scope loop). Future scope-matching changes (e.g. adding scope inheritance or wildcard scopes) must be applied in three drifting copies in this one class; the next change gets riskier because a missed copy yields inconsistent authorization results between per-client and all-clients paths.

[ADVISORY] getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken) is a private method whose only plausible caller, canExchangeTo, is overridden to throw UnsupportedOperationException, leaving dead code in the new class. Readers and future maintainers of the V2 evaluator will assume token-exchange evaluation is implemented here and either rely on it or waste effort preserving it; it should be deleted along with the now-unused ClientModelIdentity/DefaultEvaluationContext imports.

[BUG] setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean) unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException, and the ClientRemovedEvent handler in AdminPermissions.registerListener calls clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false) when a client is deleted, so with ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V2) enabled every client deletion path that goes through MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() throws. Deleting a client raises UnsupportedOperationException inside the event listener, aborting the removal transaction or leaving the client's authz resource/permission rows orphaned; orphaned 'Clients'-type resources with attached policies keep being evaluated by getClientsWithPermission/hasPermission against a nonexistent client, and re-creating a client with the same id re-attaches stale grants.

[ADVISORY] canExchangeTo(ClientModel, ClientModel, AccessToken) throws UnsupportedOperationException instead of returning false, so the V2 evaluator cannot express a deny for token-exchange. Any token-exchange path that consults the client permission evaluator while V2 fine-grained authz is enabled gets a 500 instead of a clean 403/deny, an availability defect on an authn/authz-critical flow and a silent behavioral change for existing deployments relying on per-client token-exchange permissions.

[ADVISORY] The RoleRemovedEvent/ClientRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent permission-cleanup listener is now gated behind Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ), so when the feature is disabled (including after previously being enabled) no cleanup of permission resources or policies runs on entity removal. An admin who disables the feature leaves orphaned authorization resources/policies in the store; if the feature is later re-enabled, stale grants tied to removed roles/clients/groups (or re-created entities reusing ids) are evaluated as if still valid, re-granting access that the removal was meant to revoke.

[ADVISORY] resolveClient falls back to getClientByClientId(realm, id) after the internal-id lookup, so the resource-name resolution accepts two different identifier spaces for the same resource. A user creating a permission can address a client by its public clientId while hasPermission(ClientModel, scope) looks up the resource strictly by client.getId() (ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, findByName(server, client.getId(), ...)); if the two resolution paths ever disagree on which client an id denotes (e.g. an admin creates a client whose clientId collides with another client's UUID-formatted internal id), a permission created for one client is enforced against the other, an authorization-scope confusion between tenants of the same realm.

[ADVISORY] The new canMapClientScopeRoles(ClientModel) / MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE permission path has zero test coverage: PermissionClientTest's testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient grants and exercises MAP_ROLES and MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE but never imports or uses MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE, so the scope newly added to the schema and to ClientPermissionsV2 (hasPermission(client, MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE)) is never evaluated by any test in the diff. A regression in the client-scope role-mapping permission (e.g. it always returning true, granting unauthorized role-mapping on client scopes) would pass the entire diff's test suite; users whose client-scope role mappings should be restricted get unrestricted access with no test failing.

[ADVISORY] The canManage(ClientScopeModel clientScope) override discards its parameter and delegates to canManageClientScopes() (an all-clients check), so per-client-scope permission grants are silently ignored — a new V2 branch that no test in the diff exercises (PermissionClientTest never calls any client-scope management endpoint). An admin granted MANAGE on a single client scope via a fine-grained permission will receive 403 on that client scope because only the coarse all-clients path is consulted, and no test distinguishes coarse from per-scope behavior to catch the dropped parameter.

[ADVISORY] The listener rewrite that gates all permission-cleanup events on Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ), and the new gate's interplay with the newly-added ClientRemovedEvent handling, has no test anywhere in the diff — none of the modified test files (PermissionClientTest, UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest, PermissionRESTTest) reference registerListener, ProviderEventListener, or role/client/group removal cleanup. If the feature gate misfires (e.g. Profile.isFeatureEnabled evaluating before config is ready, or the inverted condition disabling cleanup when the feature IS enabled), stale authorization resources/policies accumulate on every client/role/group removal with no failing test to signal it; the checked test files were PermissionClientTest.java, UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java, PermissionRESTTest.java, and AbstractPermissionTest.java, none covering this path.

[ADVISORY] testViewAllClients asserts getProtocolMappers().getMappers() is empty, but the test never successfully created any protocol mapper (the earlier createMapper call was asserted FORBIDDEN), so this assertion verifies an empty list that is trivially true regardless of the VIEW permission logic — it is a false-confidence assertion that would pass even if permission evaluation wrongly denied or wrongly returned another client's mappers. A future regression where getMappers() leaks mappers from other clients or bypasses permission filtering would not be caught here because the test data contains no mappers to leak; the assertion pins nothing about authorization behavior.

[ADVISORY] testViewAllClients' final negative check 'can't create a new client' calls clients().create(null), which asserts FORBIDDEN on a null-body request — the assertion can pass for the wrong reason (null validation or authz ordering) rather than verifying that a VIEW-only grant lacks MANAGE, since no valid ClientRepresentation is ever submitted. If the server ever returns 400 for the null body before reaching permission evaluation (or already does in some configurations), the test fails spuriously; conversely it does not actually demonstrate that VIEW-without-MANAGE denies creation with a real payload, so the denial behavior it claims to verify is not exercised.

[BUG] ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean) throws UnsupportedOperationException, so the ClientRemovedEvent cleanup path in AdminPermissions.registerListener crashes and leaves orphaned permission resources behind when a client is deleted. AdminPermissions.java's listener calls management(session, realm).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false) on every ClientRemovedEvent when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled; under the V2 evaluator this throws UnsupportedOperationException, aborting the client-removal event handling mid-flight and permanently orphaning the deleted client's authz Resource/Policy rows in the resource server — data that no later cleanup path in this diff removes (no cascade/migration compensates), leaving unremovable zombie authorization state that subsequent permission listings (e.g. getClientsWithPermission iterating resources of type Clients) will surface for a nonexistent client.

[BUG] ClientPermissionsV2.isPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel) throws UnsupportedOperationException even though it is a read API inherited from the shipped ClientPermissions contract, so any existing caller in the codebase or out-of-tree extension gets a runtime crash instead of a boolean during the V1→V2 transition. This is a silent public-surface/contract break on the shared base class: existing code that queries isPermissionsEnabled (admin console client representations expose permissionsEnabled) will throw UnsupportedOperationException with a 500 rather than a graceful value, so enabling the V2 path breaks readers of per-client permission state with no expand/contract phase where the old implementation remains callable.

[ADVISORY] hasPermission(ClientModel, String) dereferences the fallback resource from getResourceTypeResource without a null check before calling authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource). When no per-client resource exists and the realm's all-clients type resource has never been created (fresh realm before any permission was configured), getResourceTypeResource's create path returns null and findByResource is invoked with a null resource, throwing NPE and turning canManage/canView into a 500 instead of a plain 'false' — the admin API for that client becomes unavailable until someone creates a Clients permission.

[BUG] ClientPermissionsV2 implements isPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions, canExchangeTo and the Policy-returning methods by throwing UnsupportedOperationException, so every existing V1 call site that unconditionally probes these (token-exchange 'to' client checks, admin REST client permission subresources, permission-enabled guards) now throws a raw UnsupportedOperationException instead of returning a boolean/empty value. With the V2 evaluator active, any request path that calls clients().isPermissionsEnabled(client) or canExchangeTo(...) before checking the feature flag returns HTTP 500 from an internal UnsupportedOperationException rather than a permission decision — a raw 500 where the code previously returned false and the operation proceeded/403'd.

[ADVISORY] The removal-cleanup listener (RoleRemovedEvent / ClientRemovedEvent / GroupRemovedEvent) is now gated on Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ), so when the feature is disabled after permissions were created, deletion of a client/role/group skips setPermissionsEnabled(x, false) entirely. Operators who disable the feature on a realm that previously had fine-grained permissions enabled accumulate orphaned authz resources/policies for deleted clients, roles and groups — silent stale state with no log and no error, and re-enabling the feature surfaces grants referencing entities that no longer exist.

[ADVISORY] getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken) and the static import of TOKEN_EXCHANGE are dead code in this class — the only method that would use them, canExchangeTo, is implemented as a throw, so the helper is unreachable. Future maintainers editing token-exchange support will trip over an evaluation-context builder that is never invoked and a static import for a constant no longer referenced; the dead block and import can be deleted outright.

[ADVISORY] getClientsWithPermission issues one full policy evaluation (root.evaluatePermission) per Clients-typed resource synchronously inside the resourceStore.findByType callback, with no bound or caching. Admin list endpoints that filter by this set in a realm with many client-permission resources perform N policy evaluations per request; a realm with thousands of per-client resources turns every list call into a seconds-long DB+evaluation loop for the admin UI.

goldens.comment: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.

In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.

In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.
Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called

adjudication.rationale: In `AdminPermissions.registerListener` the `ClientRemovedEvent` branch (now inside `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ))`) calls `management(session, realm).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false);`. The finding’s specific phrasing about hasPermission() using client.getId() is somewhat off (resolveClient returns client.getId() in all cases), but the diff still shows a real access-control confusion risk introduced by accepting both ID forms with a precedence rule.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new canMapClientScopeRoles(ClientModel) / MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE permission path has zero test coverage: PermissionClientTest's testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient grants and exercises MAP_ROLES and MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE but never imports or uses MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE, so the scope newly added to the schema and to ClientPermissionsV2 (hasPermission(client, MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE)) is never evaluated by any test in the diff. A regression in the client-scope role-mapping permission (e.g. it always returning true, granting unauthorized role-mapping on client scopes) would pass the entire diff's test suite; users whose client-scope role mappings should be restricted get unrestricted access with no test failing.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new scope constant and schema entry for client permissions (AdminPermissionsSchema.MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE and CLIENTS ResourceType scopes), and wires it into authorization checks via ClientPermissionsV2.canMapClientScopeRoles(ClientModel) -> hasPermission(client, AdminPermissionsSchema.MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE). In the updated/added tests (notably PermissionClientTest.testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient), the granted client scopes are Set.of(MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, CONFIGURE) and the file’s static imports include MAP_ROLES and MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE but not MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE, and no test in the shown diff exercises canMapClientScopeRoles / MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE evaluation. This is a concrete missing-test issue for newly added nontrivial permission logic, but not a directly verifiable functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The canManage(ClientScopeModel clientScope) override discards its parameter and delegates to canManageClientScopes() (an all-clients check), so per-client-scope permission grants are silently ignored — a new V2 branch that no test in the diff exercises (PermissionClientTest never calls any client-scope management endpoint). An admin granted MANAGE on a single client scope via a fine-grained permission will receive 403 on that client scope because only the coarse all-clients path is consulted, and no test distinguishes coarse from per-scope behavior to catch the dropped parameter.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `ClientPermissionsV2.canManage(ClientScopeModel clientScope)` ignores its parameter and returns `canManageClientScopes()`, but the finding’s core claim (that *per-client-scope fine-grained permission grants* exist and are being silently ignored) is not supported by the diff. The schema changes add a new `CLIENTS` resource type/scopes (in `AdminPermissionsSchema`), but nothing introduces a resource type or permission model for individual `ClientScopeModel` objects. Also, the updated Javadoc on `ClientPermissionEvaluator#canManage(ClientScopeModel)` explicitly describes only coarse checks (admin role or V2 permission to `AdminPermissionsSchema#MANAGE`), which aligns with delegating to `canManageClientScopes()`. While it’s true the new tests don’t hit client-scope *entity* management endpoints, the asserted behavioral bug about per-scope grants causing 403 cannot be verified from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The listener rewrite that gates all permission-cleanup events on Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ), and the new gate's interplay with the newly-added ClientRemovedEvent handling, has no test anywhere in the diff — none of the modified test files (PermissionClientTest, UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest, PermissionRESTTest) reference registerListener, ProviderEventListener, or role/client/group removal cleanup. If the feature gate misfires (e.g. Profile.isFeatureEnabled evaluating before config is ready, or the inverted condition disabling cleanup when the feature IS enabled), stale authorization resources/policies accumulate on every client/role/group removal with no failing test to signal it; the checked test files were PermissionClientTest.java, UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java, PermissionRESTTest.java, and AbstractPermissionTest.java, none covering this path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes AdminPermissions.registerListener() so that RoleRemovedEvent / ClientRemovedEvent / GroupRemovedEvent cleanup only runs when Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) is true (services/.../AdminPermissions.java). This is nontrivial behavioral gating that could affect cleanup on removals, and none of the modified/added tests exercise removal events or the listener path (tests touch permission evaluation/creation, not ProviderEventManager/registerListener or removal-driven cleanup). The concern is diff-grounded as a missing test for the new feature-flag gate and added/remapped cleanup handling, but the diff alone doesn’t prove the gate is wrong (so not a verifiable bug).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] testViewAllClients asserts getProtocolMappers().getMappers() is empty, but the test never successfully created any protocol mapper (the earlier createMapper call was asserted FORBIDDEN), so this assertion verifies an empty list that is trivially true regardless of the VIEW permission logic — it is a false-confidence assertion that would pass even if permission evaluation wrongly denied or wrongly returned another client's mappers. A future regression where getMappers() leaks mappers from other clients or bypasses permission filtering would not be caught here because the test data contains no mappers to leak; the assertion pins nothing about authorization behavior.

adjudication.rationale: In `PermissionClientTest#testViewAllClients`, the test first asserts that creating a protocol mapper is forbidden, then later (after granting VIEW on all clients) calls `getProtocolMappers().getMappers()` and asserts the returned list is `empty()`. The diff shows the test never successfully creates any protocol mapper data for `myclient` (the only `createMapper` attempt is asserted FORBIDDEN), so the `empty()` assertion does not meaningfully validate authorization behavior beyond “call succeeded and returned whatever happens to be there”. If the test realm/client is initialized with no mappers (which the test itself does not change), `empty()` is effectively a weak/trivial check and wouldn’t catch leaks/misbinding to other clients’ mappers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] testViewAllClients' final negative check 'can't create a new client' calls clients().create(null), which asserts FORBIDDEN on a null-body request — the assertion can pass for the wrong reason (null validation or authz ordering) rather than verifying that a VIEW-only grant lacks MANAGE, since no valid ClientRepresentation is ever submitted. If the server ever returns 400 for the null body before reaching permission evaluation (or already does in some configurations), the test fails spuriously; conversely it does not actually demonstrate that VIEW-without-MANAGE denies creation with a real payload, so the denial behavior it claims to verify is not exercised.

adjudication.rationale: In PermissionClientTest#testViewAllClients, the final negative assertion does `realmAdminClient.realm(realm.getName()).clients().create(null)` and expects `Status.FORBIDDEN` (see added block near the end of the test). Because the request body is explicitly `null`, the test is not actually exercising “VIEW without MANAGE denies create with a valid payload”; it can fail or pass for reasons unrelated to authorization (e.g., null/validation handling or request processing order). This is a real, diff-grounded test-quality issue but not a product defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean) throws UnsupportedOperationException, so the ClientRemovedEvent cleanup path in AdminPermissions.registerListener crashes and leaves orphaned permission resources behind when a client is deleted. AdminPermissions.java's listener calls management(session, realm).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false) on every ClientRemovedEvent when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled; under the V2 evaluator this throws UnsupportedOperationException, aborting the client-removal event handling mid-flight and permanently orphaning the deleted client's authz Resource/Policy rows in the resource server — data that no later cleanup path in this diff removes (no cascade/migration compensates), leaving unremovable zombie authorization state that subsequent permission listings (e.g. getClientsWithPermission iterating resources of type Clients) will surface for a nonexistent client.

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes AdminPermissions.registerListener() call management(session, realm).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false) on every ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled. In the same diff, MgmtPermissionsV2 overrides clients() to return ClientPermissionsV2, and ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean) explicitly throws UnsupportedOperationException. If the V2 management implementation is in effect for this listener (as implied by introducing MgmtPermissionsV2/ClientPermissionsV2 for the feature), a client removal event will trigger an exception in the listener instead of performing cleanup. The claim about leaving orphaned authz state is consistent with this cleanup call being the only shown removal hook, but even without proving the DB effect, the event-handling crash is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] ClientPermissionsV2.isPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel) throws UnsupportedOperationException even though it is a read API inherited from the shipped ClientPermissions contract, so any existing caller in the codebase or out-of-tree extension gets a runtime crash instead of a boolean during the V1→V2 transition. This is a silent public-surface/contract break on the shared base class: existing code that queries isPermissionsEnabled (admin console client representations expose permissionsEnabled) will throw UnsupportedOperationException with a 500 rather than a graceful value, so enabling the V2 path breaks readers of per-client permission state with no expand/contract phase where the old implementation remains callable.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `ClientPermissionsV2` and overrides `isPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel)` to `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")` (same for `setPermissionsEnabled`). `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` is changed to return this new `ClientPermissionsV2`, so any code path using `MgmtPermissionsV2` and calling these inherited contract methods will now crash at runtime. This is not hypothetical inside the diff: `AdminPermissions.registerListener` calls `management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false)` when the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature is enabled, which would throw if `management(...)` resolves to the V2 permissions implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] hasPermission(ClientModel, String) dereferences the fallback resource from getResourceTypeResource without a null check before calling authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource). When no per-client resource exists and the realm's all-clients type resource has never been created (fresh realm before any permission was configured), getResourceTypeResource's create path returns null and findByResource is invoked with a null resource, throwing NPE and turning canManage/canView into a 500 instead of a plain 'false' — the admin API for that client becomes unavailable until someone creates a Clients permission.
matched_golden_ids: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same underlying bug: getResourceTypeResource can return null in hasPermission, and the code then calls findByResource with that null resource (dereference/usage without a null check), causing a NullPointerException. It also notes the need for defensive handling (return false vs 500), aligning with the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] ClientPermissionsV2 implements isPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions, canExchangeTo and the Policy-returning methods by throwing UnsupportedOperationException, so every existing V1 call site that unconditionally probes these (token-exchange 'to' client checks, admin REST client permission subresources, permission-enabled guards) now throws a raw UnsupportedOperationException instead of returning a boolean/empty value. With the V2 evaluator active, any request path that calls clients().isPermissionsEnabled(client) or canExchangeTo(...) before checking the feature flag returns HTTP 500 from an internal UnsupportedOperationException rather than a permission decision — a raw 500 where the code previously returned false and the operation proceeded/403'd.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `ClientPermissionsV2` overrides many inherited methods (`canExchangeTo`, all `Policy`-returning permission builders, `isPermissionsEnabled`, `setPermissionsEnabled`, `resource`, `getPermissions`) to `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")`. It also changes `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` to return this `ClientPermissionsV2` implementation. From the diff alone we cannot verify any concrete call path that will invoke these methods under V2 (no call sites are shown), so the claim that requests will now hit raw `UnsupportedOperationException`/HTTP 500 is not directly provable here. However, the change is a specific, diff-grounded risk: any existing code that calls these methods on `clients()` in V2 will now crash rather than returning a decision/value.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The removal-cleanup listener (RoleRemovedEvent / ClientRemovedEvent / GroupRemovedEvent) is now gated on Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ), so when the feature is disabled after permissions were created, deletion of a client/role/group skips setPermissionsEnabled(x, false) entirely. Operators who disable the feature on a realm that previously had fine-grained permissions enabled accumulate orphaned authz resources/policies for deleted clients, roles and groups — silent stale state with no log and no error, and re-enabling the feature surfaces grants referencing entities that no longer exist.

adjudication.rationale: In `AdminPermissions.registerListener`, the entire removal-cleanup logic for `RoleRemovedEvent`, `ClientRemovedEvent`, and `GroupRemovedEvent` was wrapped in `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)) { ... }`. Previously, `management(...).<type>().setPermissionsEnabled(<entity>, false)` ran unconditionally on those deletion events. With this diff, if the feature is disabled at deletion time, that cleanup call is skipped entirely, which can leave any previously-created fine-grained authz state uncleaned for deleted entities (at minimum a behavior regression in cleanup when toggling the feature).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken) and the static import of TOKEN_EXCHANGE are dead code in this class — the only method that would use them, canExchangeTo, is implemented as a throw, so the helper is unreachable. Future maintainers editing token-exchange support will trip over an evaluation-context builder that is never invoked and a static import for a constant no longer referenced; the dead block and import can be deleted outright.
matched_golden_ids: Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The golden issue is that the private getEvaluationContext method in ClientPermissionsV2 is unused/never called and should be removed. The candidate explicitly flags getEvaluationContext(...) as dead/unreachable code and recommends deleting it (also noting an unused static import), which is the same underlying concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] getClientsWithPermission issues one full policy evaluation (root.evaluatePermission) per Clients-typed resource synchronously inside the resourceStore.findByType callback, with no bound or caching. Admin list endpoints that filter by this set in a realm with many client-permission resources perform N policy evaluations per request; a realm with thousands of per-client resources turns every list call into a seconds-long DB+evaluation loop for the admin UI.

adjudication.rationale: The new method ClientPermissionsV2#getClientsWithPermission(String scope) iterates all resources of type AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE via resourceStore.findByType(..., callback). Inside the callback it calls hasGrantedPermission(resource, scope), which performs root.evaluatePermission(new ResourcePermission(...)) for each resource. This is an O(N) number of full policy evaluations per request with no visible bounding, batching, or caching in this diff, so the stated N-evaluations-per-list-call performance concern is directly supported by the added code. It’s a scalability/performance issue rather than a functional correctness defect.
